# N02 additive fixture records

All 53 N01 packages, their manifest, auxiliary files and digests remain frozen.
These additions do not change any package or component grammar.

- `bpe-trainer-vectors-v1.json`, SHA-256
  `04eadb1cd0cc65d43afb764dbe6a622646fb142dd1b93bfc516a0456d7406fbd`:
  eight independently counted Python training corpora, exact merge ranks,
  order-sensitive corpus identities, short-run visit counts and encoding IDs.
  These are small diagnostic tokenizer results, not neural training evidence.
- `field-table-errata-v2.json`, SHA-256
  `0b5064e396dcbaa365bd038fa611acb88ef9869d01edd6aa434dcbb60facd678`:
  documentation-only correction to frozen `field-table.json` SHA-256
  `a0a40785bc1e404fd33073c52225f6ad0bf18155a2d8a82059d22b67c5bcc8bf`.
  The v1 inference and BPE worksheets erroneously list 38 optimizer/RNG payload
  offsets each. Their actual components 6 and 7 are one-byte Absent records:
  only state tag 0 at offset 0 exists. Payload offsets are absent, never
  inferred from the resumable schema. The companion removes those cells and
  preserves the resumable control and every other original cell. It binds each
  package's original artifact identity; the independent witness checks actual
  records and retained/removed cells. No original table was regenerated.

The production decoder follows component schema state tags and lengths, never a
worksheet. Frozen expected-byte records are not generated by the Rust writer.
The new vector digest is asserted by both languages; the erratum digest and
state/presence rules are independently checked in Python. Golden changes require
an intentional versioned record and fresh review, never a failing-check refresh.

The tokenizer API separately bounds raw encode input (64 KiB), decoding token
IDs (65,536), decoded output (64 MiB), training allocation and work. Callers may
lower these ceilings. The larger decode bound supports valid long merged tokens
without confusing raw input length with generated output. These API limits add
no tokenizer normalization or new wire field.

Staging currently implements private Unix directories, create-new mode-0600
files, file sync, atomic no-clobber hard linking and directory sync. Unsupported
platform directory durability returns `Io` / `unsupported-directory-durability`
before writes. This is neither a generation-head journal nor a supported-platform
qualification. Incomplete task-created files remain for explicit retention;
unknown leftovers are never removed. Every future load still captures and
validates bytes rather than trusting a stable path or descriptor.

Writer preflight rejects contradictory raw tensor dtype/storage, rank/axes,
shape/byte length and separate moment-vector lengths before serialization. A
nonallocating counting pass checks wire and metadata sizes. Peak admission counts
all consumed record Vec/String capacities and accessible annotation payload
capacities, plus the one exact output and fixed overhead, for both serialization
and independent decoding. No directory Vec or growing output buffer is used;
borrowed annotations remain charged during decoding. Unrelated caller allocations
outside the supplied values/slice are outside this per-call budget.

Idempotent staging verifies and syncs the same existing file handle, then syncs
the directory. Both an already-present object and a no-clobber collision require
this data sync; a sync failure returns an error rather than a durable receipt.

`tokenizer-profile-negatives-v1.json`, SHA-256
`d6feb7ebeb2a8446008f1bcf7dbbc8ed65345dec21acd614d886c580049e8a4a`, adds two
semantic negatives for tokenizer clarification 1.0.1 without touching
`manifest.json` or any `.hex`: frozen `inference` with tokenizer component byte
20 (`normalization`) set to 1, and with byte 21 (`special_policy`) set to 2, each
with recomputed component-4 and directory SHA-256. A scratch `struct`/`hashlib`
worksheet produced them, never the witness or the Rust writer. Both languages pin
the file digest and expect `InvalidTokenizer`; Python also checks that only the
named byte and the two hashes differ from `inference`.

`n02-matrix-negatives-v1.json`, SHA-256
`1a724aa256436a1c8c2f4b95edc25513ac4b7bcff19de338ac401e238f38c966`, adds eight
single-defect semantic negatives for N02 review finding M6, without touching
`manifest.json` or any `.hex`. Each changes one field of frozen `resumable` and
recomputes that component's SHA-256 and the directory SHA-256: RNG
`next_example_cursor == example_count` (`InvalidRngOrder`); objective profile tag
and policy tag 2 (`InvalidObjective`); objective dataset, split and preparation
digests that no longer match component 7 (`InvalidRngOrder`); and a NaN and an
infinite first AdamW moment (`InvalidOptimizer`). A scratch `struct`/`hashlib`
worksheet produced them, never the witness or the Rust writer. Both languages pin
the file digest and the expected family; Python also checks that only the named
field and the two hashes differ from `resumable`. Remaining M6 items (held-out
sentinel documents in trainer input, decoder-side dtype mismatch, and probing more
legacy readers with model bytes) are not covered by this file.
